817.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The CI today is a cumulative gate model: PRs run L1/L2, the merge group runs L3, the nightly runs L4 and a release runs L5 (see the header comment of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). As the suite grows, three engineering capabilities have to be built in step:

1. **Test coverage**: the Coverage job merges only the UT and ST layers, the mocked browser E2E is not measured, and no gate reads the published coverage as an admission threshold.
2. **CI stability**: real-model E2E (L3/L4/L5) depends on external services and credentials, and occasional failures have no systematic mechanism for flake identification, isolation and tracking.
3. **Release CI efficiency**: the L5 release pipeline has no end-to-end budget of <5 hours, and the bulk data downloads (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install, dependencies, datasets) happen again on every run.

Related files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the L1–L5 pipeline: policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e jobs)
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` (real E2E; `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the L5 release)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (the case catalog and profile selection)
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`, `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy and result summaries)
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` (coverage merge and summary)

## Design Ideas

### 1. Test coverage

**Baseline** — the `releases/v0.3.0.beta` line, authoritative run at `6d3c49a`:

| metric | whole repo | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lines | 73.11% (105840/144777) | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| branches | 63.59% (39639/62335) | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| functions | 81.43% (7208/8852) | 81.43% | — |

- Weakest modules by line coverage: `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `scripts` 63.49%, `artifact-json` 63.16%, `specialist` 68.51%, `gateway` 68.40%.
- Cases: 3934 tagged — UT 3694/3806, ST 2/4, E2E 69/124; real-model 0/16, LLM judge 0/8, external 0/89, legacy 0/42.

**Gaps**

- Coverage is display-only: no gate reads it, and the `external` / `real` / `llm` classes are permanently 0.

**Plan**

1. Gate on industry health lines rather than the current 73%:

| metric | healthy | excellent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| branches | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| functions (Node) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| statements | ≥80% | — |
| new / changed code (diff on a PR) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| core paths (auth, sandbox execution, gateway, API routes) | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| per-package floor | ≥60% | — |

2. Land it in that order: diff coverage is enforced immediately (new code meets the line, existing code is not blocked), and the whole-repo figure ratchets upward and may never fall.

3. Starting gap: lines 73.11% (−6.89pt), branches 63.59% (−6.41pt), functions 81.43% (already passing). Four packages sit below the 60% floor — `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `services/runner` 0% — and each gets its own raise target.

4. Case-level coverage, not just a case count: a profile is the gate tier `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` resolves from a case's tags (`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`), and it decides which cases run at which level. Today the 16 real-model, 8 LLM-judge and 89 external cases are selected by no profile at all, so they never run and read 0 forever; every case must either be selected by a profile or explicitly marked out of scope in the tag catalog, so the omission surfaces at review time.

5. Tie cases to modules: the tagged catalog carries the case-to-module mapping, so a new module without an executing case fails the gate, and `planned / executed / passed` remains the execution view beside it.

### 2. CI stability

- Automatic failure classification: product defect / environment / external dependency / test flake.
- Flake governance: when a case's failure rate over its last N runs crosses a threshold, mark it quarantined automatically — it keeps running and recording results, but its failure no longer blocks merges, and a tracking issue is opened for the owner. It leaves quarantine once it passes N consecutive runs, so a flaky case neither freezes the queue nor silently disappears.
- No blanket retry. A case is rerun only when its failure is attributable to network jitter or an unstable gateway / upstream — connect and read timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, HTTP 429/5xx, interrupted streams. Every other failure, including a flaky real-model case, is reported as it happened and handled by the classification and quarantine above. A retry is labelled as an infrastructure retry, its count is visible per case, and sustained gateway failures beyond the retry budget are reported as an infrastructure incident rather than a test failure.
- Explore disabling the model's thinking mode, or setting the reasoning effort to its lowest level: much of the flakiness of the real-model cases comes from the randomness of the reasoning path; disabling or minimizing thinking narrows the output variance, makes the results more reproducible, and shortens per-case inference time (an efficiency win as well). The conclusion has to be backed by an A/B experiment — run both configurations N times each, compare pass rates and failure variance; if the pass rate does not regress beyond the accepted bound, fix it as a CI-only inference configuration applied to the L3/L4/L5 journeys only, leaving the product default untouched.

### 3. Release CI efficiency (<5h)

- Give the L5 pipeline a 5-hour end-to-end budget, add a timing view of actual per-job duration against that budget, and alert automatically when it is exceeded.
- Compress duration through caching (pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm are cached already), parallel test sharding (the mocked E2E matrix exists; extend it to UT/ST), and trimming redundant layers from the release profile.
- Run the real-model journeys at the lowest thinking effort: thinking off, or reasoning effort at its minimum, for L3/L4/L5 — reasoning tokens are the dominant cost of a case, so this shortens per-case latency directly. It is the same A/B switch as the stability item; here it is measured as p50/p95 duration per case against the 5-hour budget and fixed once the pass rate shows no regression.
- Data-download optimization: inventory the bulk downloads in the pipeline (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install with its virtualenv, pnpm / uv dependencies, test datasets and fixtures, model and sidecar data, Docker images, and the base images of the release binaries) and eliminate the repeated ones item by item — pre-download into `actions/cache`, use an internal mirror / CDN, prefetch in parallel with the build steps, and key the cache on lockfiles / content hashes. Track download time separately in the budget view; a rerun with a cache hit must not download the bulk again.
- Produce an L5 duration baseline report marking the top-N slowest jobs and the optimization suggestions (including the share of download time).

## Involved Public APIs

No new or changed product public APIs; all of this is CI-internal capability.

- Reuse the existing CI-internal interfaces: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...` (case selection), the `.ci-results` directory layout, and the `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs of `real-e2e.yml`.
- The new outputs (coverage report and duration baseline report) are uploaded as artifacts, following the existing artifact naming convention (e.g. `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`).

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.ci/` scripts: the policy, matrix and summary scripts are extended to emit coverage and timing data.
- `test/support/tagged`: the case catalog gains coverage-ownership and flake-marker fields.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`: a wider merge scope and a new output format.
- `release.yml`: the L5 budget check hooks into the existing `workflow_call` chain.
- No product code changes (apps/*, services/*); the model thinking-mode configuration is injected through the CI / E2E harness only and does not touch product defaults.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Coverage**: with a change of a known coverage delta, verify that the PR comment and the threshold block trigger correctly; verify the numbers are sound once the E2E layer is included.
- **Stability**: on a test branch, produce deterministic failures and random failures, and verify the classification, the quarantine isolation and the auto-issue flow; inject network jitter and gateway failures (timeout, connection reset, 429/5xx, interrupted stream) and verify the case is retried and, when it then passes, recorded as a pass with a visible retry count, while a product-defect failure is not retried; run the thinking-mode A/B experiment N times per arm, and verify that the failure variance narrows with no unacceptable pass-rate regression.
- **Efficiency**: take the last 3 release runs as the baseline, verify that the budget view times correctly and that the L5 end-to-end is <5 hours after the optimization; verify that the bulk data downloads take near-zero time on a cache hit; and record the per-case p50/p95 duration with thinking off or at its lowest, before and after.
- All of the above is CI behavior and automatable within L2; no new real-model cases are added (the existing L4/L5 journeys are reused).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Coverage is gated on the industry health lines: whole-repo lines ≥80%, branches ≥70%, functions ≥80% and statements ≥80%; new code ≥80% diff coverage; each package ≥60% and core paths ≥90%.
- [ ] Case-level coverage is closed: no case sits outside every profile, and every module maps to at least one case the gating profile actually executes.
- [ ] Flaky cases are identified and quarantined automatically; only failures caused by network jitter or an unstable gateway are retried, labelled as infrastructure retries and never applied to product defects; the thinking-mode (off / lowest) A/B experiment is concluded and, if viable, fixed as a CI-only inference configuration.
- [ ] The L5 release CI finishes end-to-end in <5 hours with in-pipeline over-budget alerts, every bulk download is cache/prefetch managed with no re-download on a cache hit, and the real-model journeys run at the lowest thinking effort with the latency gain recorded.

## Additional Information

- This is an engineering-effectiveness request; maintainers are invited to schedule it as the three sub-items above.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

当前 CI 采用累积门禁模型：PR 跑 L1/L2，merge_group 跑 L3，nightly 跑 L4，发布跑 L5（见 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 头部注释）。随着用例规模增长，三个方面的工程能力需要同步建设：

1. **用例覆盖度**：Coverage 任务只合并 UT、ST 两层，mocked browser E2E 未被度量，且没有任何门禁把已发布的覆盖度作为准入阈值。
2. **CI 稳定性**：真实模型 E2E（L3/L4/L5）依赖外部服务与凭据，偶发失败缺乏系统性的抖动识别、隔离与跟踪机制。
3. **版本 CI 效率**：L5 发布流水线尚无 <5 小时的端到端时长预算约束，大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB、依赖、数据集）在每次运行中反复发生。

相关文件：

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`（L1–L5 主流水线：policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e 等 job）
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`（真实 E2E；`profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入）
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`（L5 发布）
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`（用例目录与 profile 选择）
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`、`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`、`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`（策略与结果汇总）
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`（覆盖度合并与摘要）

## 设计思路

### 1. 用例覆盖度

**基线**——取 `releases/v0.3.0.beta` 线（authoritative，SHA `6d3c49a`）：

| 指标 | 整仓 | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 行 | 73.11%（105840/144777） | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| 分支 | 63.59%（39639/62335） | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| 函数 | 81.43%（7208/8852） | 81.43% | — |

- 行覆盖率最弱的模块：`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`scripts` 63.49%、`artifact-json` 63.16%、`specialist` 68.51%、`gateway` 68.40%。
- 用例：3934 个，UT 覆盖 3694/3806、ST 2/4、E2E 69/124；真实模型 0/16、LLM judge 0/8、external 0/89、legacy 0/42。

**问题**

- 覆盖度只用于展示，没有任何门禁读取；`external` / `real` / `llm` 三类用例恒为 0。

**方案**

1. 门禁取业界健康线，而不是当前的 73%：

| 指标 | 健康线 | 优秀线 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 行覆盖 | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 分支覆盖 | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| 函数覆盖（Node） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 语句覆盖 | ≥80% | — |
| 新增/变更代码（PR diff） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 核心链路（认证、沙箱执行、网关、API 路由） | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| 单包下限 | ≥60% | — |

2. 按上述顺序落地：diff 覆盖立即生效（新代码按健康线走，不阻塞存量），整仓数值以棘轮方式只升不降。

3. 当前差距：行 73.11%（差 6.89pt）、分支 63.59%（差 6.41pt）、函数 81.43%（已达标）。4 个包低于 60% 下限——`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`services/runner` 0%——各自设定提升目标。

4. 用例维度覆盖，而不只是用例数量：profile 指 `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` 依据用例 tag 解析出的门禁档位（`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`），它决定哪些用例在哪一层运行。目前 16 个真实模型、8 个 LLM judge、89 个 external 用例不被任何 profile 选中，等于永远不跑、永远显示 0；要求每条用例要么被某个 profile 选中，要么在 tag 目录中显式标注「不在范围」，让遗漏在评审阶段就暴露。

5. 用例与模块绑定：tag 目录维护「用例 → 模块」映射，新增模块若没有可执行用例则门禁失败；`planned / executed / passed` 作为与之并列的执行视图。

### 2. CI 稳定性提升

- 失败自动归类：产品缺陷 / 环境 / 外部依赖 / 用例抖动（flake）。
- 抖动治理（quarantine）：同一用例近 N 次运行失败率超阈值时自动标记为隔离——它继续运行并记录结果，但失败不再阻断合并，同时自动创建跟踪 issue 派给 owner；连续 N 次通过后自动解除隔离，既不冻结合并队列，也不会让用例悄悄消失。
- 不做统一重试。仅当失败可归因于网络抖动或网关、上游不稳定（连接与读取超时、连接重置、DNS 失败、HTTP 429/5xx、流中断）时才自动重跑；其他失败——包括真实模型用例本身的抖动——如实上报，交由上面的失败归类与 quarantine 处理。重试会标注为基础设施重试，用例维度可看到次数，超出重试预算的持续性网关失败按基础设施故障上报，而不是记为用例失败。
- 探索关闭或调低模型思考模式（thinking / reasoning effort 设为最低档）：真实模型用例的抖动很大程度来自推理路径的随机性，关闭/调低思考模式可收窄输出方差、提升可复现性，同时缩短单用例推理耗时（兼具效率收益）。结论需以 A/B 实验数据支撑：对比开启 vs 关闭（或最低档）两组各 N 次运行的通过率与失败方差，若通过率无可接受退化，则固化为 CI 专用推理配置，仅作用于 L3/L4/L5 journey，不影响产品默认行为。

### 3. 版本 CI 效率提升（<5hr）

- 为 L5 流水线定义端到端时长预算 5 小时，pipeline 内增加各 job 实际耗时 vs 预算的计时看板，超预算自动告警。
- 通过缓存（pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm 已有）、用例分片并行（mocked E2E matrix 已具备，推广到 UT/ST）、release profile 裁剪冗余层级来压缩时长。
- 真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行：L3/L4/L5 关闭思考或把 reasoning effort 调到最低——推理 token 是单个用例的主要开销，这一步直接缩短单用例耗时。与稳定性项共用同一组 A/B 开关，这里以每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对照 5 小时预算衡量，确认通过率无退化后固化。
- 数据下载优化：盘点流水线中的大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB 及其 virtualenv、pnpm / uv 依赖、测试数据集与 fixture、模型与 sidecar 数据、Docker 镜像、二进制基础镜像），逐项消除重复下载——预下载进 `actions/cache`、走内部镜像源 / CDN、与构建步骤并行预取、按 lockfile / 内容寻址命中缓存；下载耗时单独计时并纳入预算看板，缓存命中后的重复运行不应再产生大额下载。
- 输出 L5 耗时基线报告，标注 top-N 耗时 job 与优化建议（含下载耗时占比）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增、不修改产品公共 API；全部为 CI 内部能力。

- 复用现有 CI 内部接口：`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...`（用例选择）、`.ci-results` 结果目录格式、`real-e2e.yml` 的 `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入。
- 新增产物（覆盖度报告、耗时基线报告）统一作为 artifacts 上传，遵循现有 artifact 命名约定（如 `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`）。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `.ci/` 脚本：策略、矩阵、汇总脚本需扩展以输出覆盖度与耗时数据。
- `test/support/tagged`：用例目录需补充覆盖度归属与抖动标记字段。
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`：扩展合并范围与输出格式。
- `release.yml`：L5 预算检查嵌入现有 `workflow_call` 链。
- 不改动产品代码（apps/*、services/*）；模型思考模式配置仅通过 CI / E2E harness 注入，不影响产品默认行为。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **覆盖度**：构造已知覆盖变化的变更，验证 PR 评论与阈值拦截正确触发；验证 E2E 层纳入后报告数值合理。
- **稳定性**：在测试分支制造确定性失败与随机失败，验证分类、quarantine 隔离与自动建单流程；注入网络抖动与网关失败（超时、连接重置、429/5xx、流中断），验证用例被自动重试、重试后通过则记为通过且重试次数可见，而产品缺陷类失败不触发重试；思考模式 A/B 实验两组各跑 N 次，验证关闭/最低档下失败方差收窄且通过率无可接受退化。
- **效率**：以最近 3 次 release 运行作为基线，验证预算看板计时准确，优化后 L5 端到端 <5 小时；验证缓存命中后大额数据下载耗时趋近于零；记录关闭/最低思考强度前后每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对比。
- 上述验证均为 CI 自身行为，属于 L2 可自动化校验范围；不新增真实模型用例（复用现有 L4/L5 journey）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 覆盖度按业界健康线设门禁：整仓行 ≥80%、分支 ≥70%、函数 ≥80%、语句 ≥80%；新代码 diff 覆盖 ≥80%；单包 ≥60%、核心链路 ≥90%。
- [ ] 用例维度覆盖闭环：没有用例落在所有 profile 之外，每个模块都至少映射到一个门禁 profile 实际执行的用例。
- [ ] CI 具备抖动用例自动识别与 quarantine 机制；仅网络抖动 / 网关不稳定导致的失败自动重试，标注为基础设施重试且不适用于产品缺陷；完成模型思考模式（关闭/最低档）A/B 实验并形成结论，可行则固化为 CI 专用推理配置。
- [ ] L5 版本 CI 端到端时长 <5 小时，流水线内有超预算告警；大额数据下载全部纳入缓存/预下载管理，缓存命中后无冗余下载；真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行并记录耗时收益。

## 补充信息

- 本 issue 为工程效能类需求，建议 maintainer 按三个子项拆分任务排期。

# [Bug] /health serially awaits downstream services beyond Docker HEALTHCHECK timeout budget

## Summary

The API service's `/health` (and `/api/health`) endpoint awaits two downstream health checks **in series**: the Runner and the Memory Graph sidecar. The Runner check is bounded by an explicit 5-second `AbortSignal.timeout`, but the Memory Graph check has **no application-level timeout** in the fetch call. Docker's `HEALTHCHECK` for the API container is configured with a 5-second timeout. Under degraded downstream conditions the serial composition can therefore exceed the Docker budget, and the container can be reported `unhealthy` even though the API process itself is still live.

This issue is about the **design of the health probe composition**. It is not about the security exposure of `/health` (tracked separately in #267).

## Source locations

| Component | File | Line(s) | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/health` route (serial composition) | `services/api/src/http/index.ts` | 793–821 | Two sequential `await` calls |
| Runner health check (bounded) | `packages/executor/src/runner-client.ts` | 161–169 | `AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)` |
| Memory Graph health check (unbounded) | `packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts` | ~344 | `fetch(this.baseUrl + "/health")` with no `signal` |
| Docker HEALTHCHECK | `Dockerfile` | ~275–276 | `--interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=5` |

Relevant excerpts:

```typescript
// services/api/src/http/index.ts:793-821
if (request.method === "GET" && (url.pathname === "/health" || url.pathname === "/api/health")) {
  const runner = await runnerClient.health().catch(() => undefined);
  const memoryGraph = store.getMemoryGraphSettings().enabled
    ? await memoryGraphClient.health().catch(() => "degraded")
    : "disabled";
  // ... build response ...
  sendJson(response, 200, { ... });
  return;
}
```

```typescript
// packages/executor/src/runner-client.ts:161-169
async health(): Promise<RunnerHealth> {
  const sentAt = Date.now();
  const response = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}/health`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) });
  // ...
}
```

```typescript
// packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts (~line 344)
async health(): Promise<string> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}/health`); // no AbortSignal
    if (!response.ok) { /* ... */ return "degraded"; }
    // ...
  } catch { /* ... */ return "degraded"; }
}
```

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile (~line 275)
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=5 \
  CMD curl --silent --fail http://127.0.0.1:4310/health || exit 1
```

## Expected behavior

- The liveness probe should reflect the API process's own ability to respond within the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` timeout.
- Each downstream check should be individually bounded so that the sum of their latencies cannot exceed the probe budget.
- A slow or unresponsive downstream should report `degraded` for that component, not stall the entire `/health` response.

## Actual behavior

- The two downstream checks run in series. The total latency is `latency(runner) + latency(memoryGraph)`.
- The Runner check is bounded at 5 s.
- The Memory Graph check has **no explicit application-level timeout**. Its effective upper bound is whatever the underlying TCP / socket layer decides (connection timeout, TLS handshake, server-side idle), which is environment-dependent and not controlled by the API process.
- The Docker `HEALTHCHECK` budget is 5 s, with `--retries=5` before the container is marked `unhealthy`.

Under normal conditions the composed latency is well below 5 s. Under degraded downstream conditions (cold-starting sidecar, Neo4j under load, bind-mount I/O pressure, network congestion) the Memory Graph leg can stretch, and the composed latency can exceed the Docker budget.

## Observed correlation (not a causation claim)

In one local Windows + Docker Desktop run the Docker health history reported `FailingStreak = 18` for the API container. The serial-composition design above is a **plausible contributing factor**, but this issue does **not** claim to have proven that the Memory Graph leg was the root cause of those specific failures. Other contributors (sidecar startup ordering, Neo4j readiness, host I/O scheduling) may also be involved. The observation is recorded because it motivated the investigation; it is not offered as evidence of a specific failure mechanism.

## Risk

- **False-negative liveness**: Docker marks the API container `unhealthy` while the API process is still capable of serving requests.
- **Orchestration side effects**: depending on the deployment's `restart` policy, an `unhealthy` container may be restarted, interrupted, or removed from a load balancer — none of which are appropriate responses to a slow downstream.
- **User-visible impact**: the web client reads `/health` to populate the Memory Graph status indicator; a stalled `/health` can cause the UI to flicker between `ok` / `degraded` / `unavailable`.
- **Composable design debt**: as more downstream services are added to `/health`, the serial composition will make the probe increasingly fragile.

## Reproduction

1. Start the SD stack (`scripts/start-stack.sh` or `docker compose up`).
2. Confirm the Memory Graph sidecar is enabled in System Settings.
3. Introduce a delay on the Memory Graph's `/health` path. Two practical ways:
   - Pause the Neo4j container (`docker pause <neo4j>`), or
   - Use a traffic-shaping tool (e.g. `tc netem`) on the sidecar's network namespace to add ≥ 4 s latency.
4. In a loop, measure the API's `/health` response time:
   ```bash
   while true; do
     curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}\n" http://127.0.0.1:4310/health
     sleep 2
   done
   ```
5. Observe that the measured latency grows to match the injected delay, and that once it exceeds 5 s Docker's `HEALTHCHECK` begins to fail.
6. After `--retries=5` consecutive failures, `docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' <api-container>` reports `unhealthy`.

## Suggested directions (for upstream consideration, not prescriptive)

- **Bound the Memory Graph check**: add an `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` to the fetch call in `memory-graph.ts` so the probe is self-bounded.
- **Split liveness from readiness**: keep `/health` minimal (API process only) for Docker, and expose a separate `/ready` that composes downstream status for the UI and orchestrator.
- **Parallelize downstream checks**: if composition is kept, run the two checks with `Promise.all` so the composed latency is the max rather than the sum.
- **Make the Docker budget authoritative**: ensure the composed worst-case latency is strictly less than `HEALTHCHECK --timeout`, with headroom for OS scheduling.

## Environment where this was observed

- OS: Windows 11 (22631)
- Runtime: Docker Desktop with bind-mounted data directory (9P filesystem)
- SD build: `sd-catalystpi-probe` worktree, M4 milestone
- Memory Graph backend: Neo4j sidecar

## Relates to

- #267 — `/health` security exposure (orthogonal; this issue is about latency budget, not authentication).

# [Bug] Agent run stalls after todo_create tool.started without completion event and hits 240s idle timeout

## Summary

During a real end-to-end run on the SD stack, the agent's event stream stopped emitting progress for roughly **4 minutes 13 seconds** immediately after a `tool.started` event for the `todo_create` tool. No matching `tool.output` or `tool.completed` event was ever emitted for that invocation. The run was then terminated by the gateway's idle-timeout watchdog with the error:

```
Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms
```

This issue records the **observed fault symptom** and the associated evidence. The **internal root cause is not determined**: we do not know whether the stall happened inside the `todo_create` tool implementation, the gateway's tool-dispatch layer, the model gateway, or an underlying runtime component. Attribution to any specific component (SiliconFlow, SQLite, network, single gateway module, etc.) is intentionally **not** made here.

## Run identifiers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `a990cea3-bbf3-4e02-a0da-a4bd95237e79` |
| Session ID | `b52f69ac-eb99-4777-91ca-9aee2eb9063c` |
| Agent Run ID (evidence) | `9b87d4ab-0798-470b-bbb6-ed2c32167a65` |
| User Message ID | `ce4e1c3e-4f3b-495a-91f5-6285317c8664` |
| Model ID | `e1c88640-84b2-447c-ab9a-ef1e4604126b` |
| Skill selection mode | `all` (17 skills enabled) |
| Created at | `2026-11-03T11:14:19.514Z` |
| Started at | `2026-11-03T11:14:38.558Z` |
| Finished at | `2026-11-03T11:21:05.622Z` |
| Final status | `failed` |
| Terminal error | `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` |

## Observed event sequence (stall window)

The SSE stream against `/api/sessions/{sid}/messages` (with `Accept: text/event-stream`) delivered the following frames around the stall window. All timestamps are UTC on 2026-11-03. `id` is the SSE sequence id; `receivedAt` is the client-side receive timestamp.

| SSE id | receivedAt | type | detail | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 149 | 11:16:27.313 | `agent.record` | `model.completed` (turn 1) | last model-completed record before tool call |
| 150 | 11:16:27.394 | `assistant.response.settled` | turn 2 | LLM response stream closed |
| **151** | **11:16:27.402** | **`tool.started`** | **`todo_create` (status `running`)** | **last normal progress event** |
| — | *11:16:27.402 – 11:20:40.144* | — | **no SSE frames received** | **~4 min 13 s stall window** |
| **152** | **11:20:40.144** | **`agent.record`** | **`state.committed`** | first event after stall window |
| **153** | **11:21:05.507** | **`run.failed`** | `error: "Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms"`, `errorCode: timeout` | terminal failure |
| 154 | 11:21:05.712 | `run.status` | `status: failed` | final state notification |

### What is missing

For every observed `tool.started` earlier in the same run, the stream delivered a matching `tool.output` (sometimes with a `null` SSE id) and a `tool.completed` within seconds:

| Tool | tool.started id | tool.output | tool.completed id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rename_session` | 98 | line 99 (null id) | 99 |
| `list_files` | 100 | line 102 (null id) | 101 |
| **`todo_create`** | **151** | **— missing —** | **— missing —** |

The `todo_create` invocation is the only tool call in this run whose lifecycle is not closed.

## Evidence

- **Raw SSE capture**: `raw_sse.jsonl` (156 lines, covering SSE ids 1–154 plus two `tool.output` frames with null ids). The stall-window excerpt above is taken verbatim from this file.
- **Run final status**: `run_final_status.json` reports `status: failed`, `error: "Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms"`, `finishedAt: 2026-11-03T11:21:05.622Z`.
- **Idle-timeout source**: `services/api/src/agent-run/run-deadlines.ts` implements a dual deadline (turn + idle). The idle deadline is rearmed by `progress()` on every gateway event; if no progress is reported for `idleMs` (240 000 ms in this run), `expire("idle")` fires and the run is failed with the message observed above.
- **Progress trigger sites**: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` calls `markProgress()` from the SSE `emit()` path, the model-gateway progress path, the `run_started` path, and adapter events. During the stall window, none of these sites fired, consistent with the SSE stream going silent.

## Expected behavior

- A `tool.started` event should be followed by a `tool.output` and a `tool.completed` (or a `tool.failed`) within a bounded, reasonable interval.
- If a tool invocation cannot complete, the gateway should either time it out at a tool-level budget or surface a `tool.failed` event, so the run can terminate cleanly with an attributable cause.
- The idle watchdog should fire only when the gateway as a whole has truly stopped making progress, not as the primary symptom of a single tool hanging.

## Actual behavior

- After `tool.started(todo_create)` at 11:16:27.402Z, no further progress event was emitted for 4 min 13 s.
- No `tool.output` or `tool.completed` for `todo_create` was ever emitted.
- The idle watchdog fired at the 240 s budget and terminated the run with a generic stall error.
- The first post-stall event (`agent.record state.committed`) arrived 13 s after the inferred watchdog expiry; the terminal `run.failed` arrived 25 s after that.

## Impact

- The run's scientific work in progress (turn 1 of a multi-turn research plan) was lost.
- The user-visible error message (`no gateway progress for 240000 ms`) does not identify which component stalled, which makes self-diagnosis difficult.
- The missing tool lifecycle events make post-mortem attribution impossible from the SSE stream alone.

## Reproduction

1. Start the SD stack (`scripts/start-stack.sh` or `docker compose up`) on any host.
2. Create a project and a session.
3. Enable the default skill set (17 skills, including the one that exposes `todo_create`).
4. Send the following prompt (the same prompt used in the affected run):

   > 我正在研究 Pd 催化 1,3-二烯的选择性发散反应，希望理解不同配体、溶剂和 CO 条件如何影响羰基化与分子内环化路径。请识别关键科学问题、已知信息和未知信息，制定可执行的研究计划，并说明哪些步骤需要文献、计算或实验支持。不要直接给出未经验证的机理结论。

5. Open an SSE connection to `/api/sessions/{sid}/messages` with `Accept: text/event-stream`.
6. Observe whether a `tool.started` for `todo_create` is followed by matching `tool.output` / `tool.completed` events, or whether the stream stalls for minutes and ends with `run.failed` / `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms`.

The fault is **intermittent** in our experience: the same stack and prompt do not reproduce the stall on every run. That is part of what makes the issue worth tracking upstream — the manifestation is real, the trigger is not yet isolated.

## Environment where this was observed

- OS: Windows 11 (22631)
- Runtime: Docker Desktop with bind-mounted data directory (9P filesystem)
- SD build: `sd-catalystpi-probe` worktree, M4 milestone
- Model gateway: SiliconFlow (external LLM provider, via the SD model-gateway layer)
- Memory Graph backend: Neo4j sidecar

## What this issue is NOT claiming

- It does **not** attribute the stall to SiliconFlow, the model gateway, SQLite, the memory-graph sidecar, the network, or any single gateway component.
- It does **not** claim that the idle watchdog is wrong to fire; the watchdog behaved as designed. The question is why no progress was reported for 240 s.
- It does **not** claim that the stall is deterministically reproducible from the prompt alone.

## Suggested investigations (for upstream, not prescriptive)

- Add tool-lifecycle logging on the gateway: for every `tool.started`, record the matching `tool.output` / `tool.completed` / `tool.failed` and the elapsed time, even when the run is later terminated by the idle watchdog.
- Add a per-tool execution budget, independent of the run-level idle timeout, so a single hanging tool fails the tool rather than the whole run.
- Surface the stalled tool's name in the terminal `run.failed` error message, so users and operators can attribute the fault without replaying the SSE stream.
- Correlate this run's gateway-side logs (model-gateway requests, tool dispatch, adapter events) with the SSE capture to identify where the `todo_create` invocation stopped making progress.

## Relates to

- Issue A (same submission batch) — `/health` serial-composition design. Orthogonal; the two issues share the same local test environment but do not share a causal link.

### 🚀 Background Description

ScienceDiscovery 已支持 Agent 在对话中选择已注册模型、调整思考参数、选择 Skill／Library、启用已就绪连接器和调整会话审阅偏好。其他设置仍需切换到设置页。本轮将下列设置接入同一套对话提案和配置卡流程，使用户可以核对当前值、拟议变更及其生效范围，并在对话中完成确认。

### Design Ideas

复用正式配置服务和既有配置卡。Agent 根据当前值、继承来源和可选项生成有限字段的提案。用户确认后写入对应的部署、共享资源、Project 或 Session 设置。权限和安全策略需要独立人工确认。密钥通过专用安全输入，预览和回执只展示非敏感信息，涉及凭据的接收地址单独确认。保存、外部服务连通性、鉴权、重启和后续任务生效分别验证。

- #727 包源和 Runner。选择已有 pip／conda 预设，在 Project／Session 分配或停用已注册 Runner。
- #734 代理。管理共享代理资源，设置供应商和 MCP 的代理选择，部署默认路由变更需独立安全确认。
- #737 Web 搜索与凭据。按 Native／JiuwenSwarm 的支持范围调整搜索、抓取和缓存，安全替换或清除已支持供应商的 Key。
- #756 审阅、探索树、JSON 与继承。调整 Reviewer 参与，选择已注册探索树模板及受支持的强度和预算，开关 JSON 专用预览，让有限的 Project／Session 普通配置恢复继承。
- #758 安全和审批。调整沙箱网络、当前会话审批、新会话默认审批和低风险自动保存策略，每类策略都需独立人工确认。
- #763 模型和供应商。编辑已有模型的元数据和 API 身份、共享供应商连接及其凭据，保存前复核实际接收地址。
- #770 Memory 和 Neo4j。调整工作台记忆图谱开关、local／Neo4j 后端、连接地址和用户名，单独替换或清除 Neo4j 密码。
- #773 已有 MCP。调整已注册服务器的元数据、超时、启用状态和受支持的覆盖项，安全替换已有凭据 header，删除自定义服务器需单独确认。

### Involved Public APIs

Base: 865102a336d9
At: 2026-11-04T00:04:46Z

## What happens

The fix that landed for the desktop composer (#794 / #804) introduced a single predicate, `commitsOnEnter`, and wired three desktop call sites to it. Six Enter handlers were left behind, and two of the guards that exist are only half a guard. With a Chinese / Japanese / Korean IME the Enter that accepts a candidate still reaches them.

Unguarded on `main` `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c`:

| Site | What the composition Enter does today |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/SshKeyFileField.tsx:83` | calls `browse()`, so the dialog leaves the directory the user was typing |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/RunnerResources.tsx:588` | sends a second `GET /api/remote-hosts/key-files` for the half-typed path (1 → 2 requests) |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx:158` | commits the timeout field with the pinyin still in it |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:199` | applies the highlighted model-listing entry, so the field becomes a value the user did not choose |

Guarded, but only against one of the two shapes an engine reports:

```tsx
// apps/web/src/session/ManagementControls.tsx:66
if (event.key !== "Enter" || event.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;
// apps/web/src/App.tsx:5051
if (event.key !== "Enter" || event.shiftKey || event.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;
```

These read `nativeEvent.isComposing` only. An engine that reports the confirming Enter as `keyCode === 229` without setting `isComposing` (notably on Windows) gets past both, and neither reads a top-level `isComposing` on a bare `KeyboardEvent`.

Both shapes are what `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts` already handles:

```ts
if (event.isComposing === true || event.nativeEvent?.isComposing === true) return false;
if (event.keyCode === 229) return false;
```

Five more handlers share an `Enter`/`Space` branch that only selects or activates something and commits no data (`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphView.tsx:155`, `apps/web/src/IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx:287`, `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:528`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolIoBlock.tsx:69`, `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ListSelect.tsx:167`). They are listed so the sweep is reproducible, not to change them.

## Expected

An Enter whose keydown belongs to an open composition must not drive a browse, a request, a field commit or a listing pick, in either app. After the composition ends, Enter behaves exactly as it does today, and `Shift+Enter` keeps the meaning each call site already gives it.

## Evidence

Reproduced on `main` `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c` by rendering the real components with a synthetic keydown carrying `isComposing: true`, `nativeEvent.isComposing: true` and `keyCode: 229`, then the same keydown with `isComposing: false` and `keyCode: 13` as the control.

Web `SshKeyFileField`, the dialog leaves the typed directory:

```
not ok 1 - SshKeyFileField: Enter while an IME is composing must not drive browse()
    a composition Enter must not trigger a browse
    + actual - expected
    + [
    +   '~/.ssh'
    + ]
    - []
```

Desktop `RunnerResources` key-file browser, two requests for one Enter:

```
not ok 1 - desktop SshKeyFileField: Enter while an IME is composing must not browse()
    a composition Enter must not trigger a browse
    2 !== 1
```

Desktop `ModelForm` model listing, a value the user did not pick:

```
not ok 1 - ModelForm combobox: Enter while an IME is composing must not apply a listing entry
    a composition Enter must not apply a listing entry
    'gpt-4o-mini' !== ''
```

Desktop `Timeouts` timeout field, committed without the field ever blurring:

```
not ok 1 - desktop timeout field: Enter while an IME is composing must not commit the field
    a composition Enter must not commit the field
    false !== true
```

Web `ManagementControls` rename, the half-guard the composition flag does not reach — this keydown sets `keyCode: 229` while both `isComposing` flags stay false:

```
not ok 1 - InlineRenameInput: Enter while an IME is composing must not commit the rename
    a composition Enter must not blur the rename field
    false !== true
```

The control case (composition already ended) is green in every one of them, so the failure is the composing path and not the probe.

## Why this is not covered by #804

`#804` changed `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx`, `PromptDialog.tsx` and `Sidebar.tsx` only. `apps/web` keeps its own call sites and never imports from `apps/desktop`, and the two `nativeEvent.isComposing` guards above were already there before that PR, which is what made them look done.

## Acceptance

- Every Enter handler that commits, sends, requests or picks reads one predicate per app: the existing `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts` for desktop, and the same predicate in `apps/web` for web, with the two copies kept character-for-character identical and each covered by the same set of unit cases.
- Each of the six sites above has a test that fails on the composition keydown and passes on the post-composition one.
- The five select/activate handlers stay unchanged, and the pull request says why.
- `git grep` for a bare `Enter` keydown comparison in `apps/web/src` and `apps/desktop/src` returns only those five, so a later reader can re-run the sweep the same way.
- Both apps' existing suites stay green.

Branch: dev1/fix/csv-parsed-extra-column
Base: 865102a336d9
At: 2026-11-04T00:05:36Z

## What happens

Two things go wrong in the CSV/TSV importer, both from deciding the table's columns from the rows instead of from the header line:

1. **A column appears that is not in the file.** When a row has more cells than the header, Papa Parse parks the surplus cells on the record under its internal key `__parsed_extra`, and the importer turns that key into a real column titled `__parsed_extra` — sortable, typed, exported. With one surplus cell the value is a plain number; with two or more it is the cells joined by commas (`"3,4"`), i.e. a value the file never contained.
2. **A column that is in the file can vanish.** When no row fills a header column, the row-key union has no such key and the column is absent from `columns` altogether — not empty, not hidden: it cannot be seen, charted or exported.

On `main` `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c`, `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`:

- `:210` parses with `header: true` (`:212`), so a record wider than the header cannot be keyed by name.
- `:108` decides the columns from the union of the row keys, excluding exactly one synthetic key:

```ts
const fields = [...new Set(rows.flatMap((row) => Object.keys(row)).filter((field) => field !== "__rowId"))];
```

- `:222` does read the real header (`fields = result.meta.fields ?? []`), but only hands it to `inferTableKind`, never to the column list.
- `:157`/`:158` then build a `ColumnProfile` per key, and `VirtualDataTable.tsx:96` renders `column.id` as the header text (`:95` puts it in the sort button's title), so the reader sees the literal key.

The same function is the import path for every CSV/TSV artifact, before anything renders, so no viewer-level workaround exists.

## Steps to reproduce

Any CSV with a row wider or narrower than its header line — no quoting, BOM or header trick involved:

```
a,b
1,2,3
```

and, for the missing-column half:

```
a,b,c
1,2
```

## Expected

The table shows the file's own columns, in the header's order, under the header's own names. Surplus cells never become a column of their own: if they are still shown, they are shown under a header cell that is visibly empty — the way the API's delimited preview already reports a column with no name — never under a name the file did not write. A header column stays present when every row is short of it.

## Actual

Run through the importer itself (`parseCsvText`, `apps/web` at `bd8423b8`), not through Papa Parse directly:

```
=== extra cells (3 in a 2-column row) ===
content: "a,b\n1,2,3\n"
columns: [{"id":"a","label":"a"},{"id":"b","label":"b"},{"id":"__parsed_extra","label":"  parsed extra"}]
rows: [{"__rowId":"row-2","a":1,"b":2,"__parsed_extra":3}]
warnings: ["Row 2: Too many fields: expected 2 fields but parsed 3"]

=== two extra cells (4 in a 2-column row) ===
content: "a,b\n1,2,3,4\n"
columns: [{"id":"a","label":"a"},{"id":"b","label":"b"},{"id":"__parsed_extra","label":"  parsed extra"}]
rows: [{"__rowId":"row-2","a":1,"b":2,"__parsed_extra":"3,4"}]
warnings: ["Row 2: Too many fields: expected 2 fields but parsed 4"]

=== short row (1 in a 3-column row) ===
content: "a,b,c\n1,2\n"
columns: [{"id":"a","label":"a"},{"id":"b","label":"b"}]
rows: [{"__rowId":"row-2","a":1,"b":2}]
warnings: ["Row 2: Too few fields: expected 3 fields but parsed 2"]
```

So `c` is not merely empty in the third case: it is not a column at all, and `3` in the first case is a column of its own headed `__parsed_extra`. The header cell renders that id verbatim (`VirtualDataTable.tsx:96`); the `label` above is not what the table shows. With `a,,c` (an empty name in the header) the importer already produces a column whose id and label are both `""` and the viewer renders it as a nameless column — so an unnamed column is a shape this table already supports and renders correctly.

## Why it matters

The CSV importer is how a reader's own file becomes a table, and the grid is what they trust for "which value belongs to which column". Here a real value is moved out of its position (`3` in `1,2,3` was under no header), presented as `"3,4"` or as a column named after a library internal, and a version of the same file with an empty column silently loses that column from the viewer, the chart field list and the CSV export.

There *is* a per-row warning (`Too many fields: expected 2 fields but parsed 3`) on the table, so the raggedness is not entirely silent — but it reads as a property of the row, and nothing says a column was invented or dropped.

## Known boundaries

- A header that literally contains `__parsed_extra` is not recoverable: Papa Parse overwrites that key with its own bucket, so the two cannot be told apart. Such a column will read empty while its values land in the surplus columns. This is a pre-existing library collision, not something this fix introduces.
- `DataRow` keys must be unique, so the surplus columns need synthetic ids. A synthetic id that collides with a real header name is suffixed (`__extra_1_`) to stay unique. Ids are internal: with the header cell rendering empty for a column that has no reader-facing name, the synthetic id is not what a reader sees.
- The exported header row goes through the same formula neutralisation as the cells, because in the positional shape a header name is a data value. So a legitimate header that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` also gets the `'` prefix — `-log2FC,b` exports as `'-log2FC,b`. That is deliberate: Excel reads `-log2FC` as a formula, and the prefix is the standard text marker (spreadsheet apps do not display it). Splitting the rule per column kind would put the header and its own cells under two different policies.

## Scope

- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`: `__parsed_extra` must never become a field. Keep the values rather than drop them, matching the API's delimited preview: table width becomes `max(header count, widest returned row)`, the header's own names stay first and in the file's order (taken from `meta.fields`), surplus columns get synthetic ids (`__extra_1`, `__extra_2`, …) with `label: ""`, and a short row keeps every header column (`null` for the cells it did not have, which is the same value an empty cell already produces today). `profileRows` currently derives the column order from the row-key union at `:108`; it needs an optional ordered column list so a surplus column filled by only some rows does not come and go, and so a header column no row fills is still present.
- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx:214`: the export has to become positional. It currently calls `rowsToCsv(rows, table.columns.map((column) => column.id))`, and that helper uses each field as *both* the value key and the header name — so handing it the header text as the field would read `row[""]` (undefined: the surplus value silently disappears from the export) and two unnamed columns would collapse onto the same object key. The fix needs a header row built from the header text and a body built cell-by-cell from `column.id`, e.g. `tableToCsv(rows, columns)` in `chart-spec/filters.ts`; `rowsToCsv` then has no production caller left and can go, with its spreadsheet-formula test moved to the new helper. Header names travel as data values in that shape, so they get the same formula neutralisation as the cells.
- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/components/VirtualDataTable.tsx:96`: render the id only when `column.label` is non-empty, and the empty string otherwise, so a column with no reader-facing name gets an empty header cell. Real header names are unaffected, because `:158` gives every real field a non-empty label. `:95`'s sort `title` keeps the id: the header cell is empty, but the sort control still needs an accessible name.
- Unit tests beside the importer in `apps/web/tests/` (its tests live there; `CsvArtifact.test.tsx` already drives the importer through the component, so a focused test may be a new file next to it): one surplus cell and two (no `__parsed_extra` id, header names and order unchanged, values still reachable), a header column that no row fills (present, `null`, `missingCount` counted), the rendered header text for an unnamed column, and the export header, plus the existing well-formed cases unchanged.
- No i18n string is added, no existing column label or header text changes, `#654`'s BOM handling of real header names is untouched, and the `rowId` de-duplication below `:108` is untouched.

Related but separate: `#650`/`#653` fixed quoting in the API preview; the API's own ragged-row normalisation is handled in `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`. This report is the web-side half, and the two should agree on the "no name, values kept" shape.

## Context

This tracks a staged landing for the work currently visible in #315 (GitCode !125), plus the two smaller follow-up branches for KE/trace integration and finish-gate refinements.

The current combined PR is 275 files and about +54k lines. Review feedback has correctly identified both the review/merge risk and the need for an explicit product decision about KE as a first-class ScienceDiscovery surface. I will preserve #315 as the full implementation reference, but stop refreshing it with large upstream merges and instead prepare clean, independently reviewable PRs from current `main`.

## Proposed landing sequence

### A. Independent research/runtime foundations

These do not require the KE service and can be reviewed on their own merits.

- [ ] **A1 — Tool-output trust boundary:** per-run nonce fencing, `untrustedCategory`, MCP remote classification, and the corresponding prompt contract. Raw stored output remains unchanged; fencing applies to model-visible content.
- [ ] **A2 — Research state:** session research state, project ledger hydration/promotion, and tournament ranking primitives.
- [ ] **A3 — Runtime controls:** native stall guard and the `TurnLifecycle.beforeFinish`/continuation event primitives. This will not claim equivalent native-style stall protection for JiuwenSwarm.
- [ ] **A4 — Session Plan:** versioned human approval, decision log, cancellation and recovery, with an explicit compatibility rule for the existing `update_plan` snapshot mechanism.
- [ ] **A5 — Finish-gate core:** skill audit and termination intervention for native and post-run/Swarm execution. The initial landing will include the already-developed fixes for loaded-skill-only audits, Swarm tool aliases, and self-referential gate/verifier text. KE grounding comes later.
- [ ] **A6 — Agent Memory:** candidate memories, human promotion, reviewed-only prompt injection, and background review. The KE LLM-helper dependency and process-global manager need to be removed first.

### B. Knowledge Engine core

- [ ] **B1 — Text/extraction/resolution domain:** pure text, JATS, extraction, and entity-resolution modules with unit tests.
- [ ] **B2 — Graph/growth/eval algorithms:** graph algorithms, gap discovery, growth selection, and evaluation primitives.
- [ ] **B3 — Persistence and ingestion data plane:** SQLite store/migrations, scholarly connectors, PDF/vision parsing, and background runners.
- [ ] **B4 — Orchestration and minimal REST:** orchestrator, grow, routes, and narrowly scoped bootstrap/http wiring. Agent tools, resident summary, graph mirror, and living review stay out of this first REST PR.
- [ ] **B5 — Minimal KE Web shell:** API client, KE page, graph canvas, and document reader.

### C. Agent integration and advanced KE surfaces

- [ ] **C1 — Consumption tools and kbScope:** KE search/expand/grep tools, session binding, web-search restrictions, resident summary, and picker. Scope enforcement lands with the first exposed tool.
- [ ] **C2 — Citation and anti-hallucination runtime:** citation verification, novelty checks, evidence ledger, report polish, and finish-gate grounding. Includes the no-available-KB advisory behavior rather than an unachievable hard lock.
- [ ] **C3 — Reports, DRIFT, and memory-graph bridge:** community reports, DRIFT search, KE-to-memory-graph mirroring, and KB deep links.

### Small follow-ups from the former KE/trace and finish-gate PRs

These can land as soon as their specific dependencies are present; they do not all need to wait for the entire base series.

- [ ] Paper presence lookup and KB badge (after minimal REST + Web).
- [ ] Explicit Paper-to-KB re-ingest (after presence lookup).
- [ ] Reviewer citation checks with a bound-KB short circuit (after citation verification + kbScope).
- [ ] KB reader back-link to the current session memory graph (after graph mirroring).
- [ ] `gap_candidates` to deduplicated `research_state` open questions (after research state + observer wiring).
- [ ] Quoting-discipline skill updates and catalog/version pins with their corresponding gate/skill stages.

## Per-stage requirements

- Each PR is cut from current `main`; mixed files such as `store.ts`, `runs/index.ts`, `http/index.ts`, and `App.tsx` are ported by focused hunks rather than copied wholesale.
- Unit/integration tests and the relevant journeys land with their feature, not in a final test-only PR.
- Current-main behavior is preserved, including catalog transaction/rollback semantics, deletion-settling shutdown, response identity, and Swarm skill-selection behavior.
- Tool trust is field-aware: deterministic verdicts must not implicitly make corpus titles, abstracts, snippets, or entity descriptions trusted.
- The fenced evidence-ledger path, post-run terminal-event ordering, and no-engine kbScope behavior receive explicit integration coverage.
- Runtime-affecting stages receive a clean deployment and real E2E validation before the next stage.

Unless maintainers prefer a dedicated integration branch, the default is small PRs directly to `main`, with at most one or two open at a time. Feedback on the staged product scope and on starting with **A1 + B1** would be appreciated.

837.author: HugoXK
837.body:
## What happens

`apps/web/tests/` holds 126 `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx` files, and no TypeScript configuration in the repository includes any of them. The suite runs under `tsx`, which strips the annotations without checking them; the package `typecheck` and the root test type-check both look elsewhere. A type error in a web test therefore cannot turn CI red: `pnpm typecheck` — the `check:typecheck` gate — stays green.

## Where

1. `apps/web/package.json:9` — `"test": "tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx"`. `tsx` transpiles and runs; it does not type-check.
2. `apps/web/tsconfig.json:9` — `"include": ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx", "vite.config.ts"]`. The package's `typecheck` script (`apps/web/package.json:10`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) therefore cannot see `tests/`.
3. `tsconfig.tests.json:23-28` — its `include` names `packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` and `services/*/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` only. Its own comment (`tsconfig.tests.json:13-15`) states: "`apps/web` is not here: its tests sit in `tests/`, which its own `include` (`src/**`) never reached, so the base exclude takes nothing away from it." The root `typecheck` script (`package.json:51`) ends with `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`, so the one configuration meant to own test files leaves the web tests out on purpose.

CI runs that script as `check:typecheck` (`test/support/tagged/checks.mjs:23` → `pnpm typecheck`), so this is a hole in a required gate, not just in a local command.

## Measured on `main` at `5c893570`

- 126 files match `apps/web/tests/*.test.ts(x)` (git tree).
- `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --listFilesOnly` lists 0 files under `apps/web/tests/`.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --listFilesOnly` lists 0 files under `apps/web/tests/` (1,805 files listed in total).
- A throwaway config extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `"exclude": []` and `"include": ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.tsx"]` lists exactly the 126 files and reports 444 `error TS` diagnostics across 71 files (10 in `.test.ts`, 434 in `.test.tsx`). Those diagnostics are latent today; nothing in CI can see them.

## How to reproduce

1. Append `const notAString: string = 42;` to any `apps/web/tests/*.test.ts`.
2. `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` — exits 0: `tsx` runs the file and never checks the annotation.
3. `pnpm typecheck` — still exits 0: neither configuration includes the file.

## Suggested fix

Give the web tests an owner and a gate:

- Add `apps/web/tsconfig.tests.json` extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `"exclude": []` and `"include": ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.tsx"]`, and run it from the package `typecheck` (or from the root `typecheck` right after `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`). Adding `apps/web/tests/**` to the root `tsconfig.tests.json` include is the alternative, but that config extends `tsconfig.base.json`, not the web package's settings, so it would need the jsx / DOM / `vite/client` options that belong to `apps/web` — a second config is the cleaner shape.
- The 444 existing diagnostics have to be fixed for the gate to pass. If that is too large for one change, stage it: enable `tests/**/*.test.ts` first (10 diagnostics) and `tests/**/*.test.tsx` (434) in a follow-up. Enabling the config while it reports errors leaves the gate red and is not mergeable.

Acceptance: with the new config wired into `pnpm typecheck`, the deliberate `const notAString: string = 42;` makes `pnpm typecheck` (and therefore `check:typecheck`) fail naming that file and line, while `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` keeps its current behaviour.

839.author: HugoXK
839.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable`) takes its width from the **widest line of the whole file**, so one outlier line decides how many columns every returned row shows. A two-column file that contains a single line with 200,001 fields renders as 1,001 columns, 999 of them carrying an empty header and an empty cell in every row.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): `const widest = lines.reduce(...)`, `const totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)` (`MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1001`), and the blank header names built at `columns: header.length >= width ? header.slice(0, width) : [...header, ...Array.from({length: width - header.length}, () => "")]`.

## Measured at `0477d328` (default `maxRows`)

- two-column header plus one line of 200,001 fields: `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {total: 200001, shown: 1001}`, rows padded to 1001 cells each, so 999 columns and ~99,900 cells in the payload are blank.
- the same file without the outlier line: `columns 2`.

## Why it matters

The preview is widened by a line that is not part of the returned rows, and the extra columns carry no header - the grid shows a two-column table as a 1,001-column one. `clippedColumns` does report `{total, shown}`, so the cut is signalled, but the blank columns themselves are still rendered.

## Suggested fix

Cap the *unnamed surplus* columns the way the CSV importer already does (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`, `surplusColumnLimit`: `min(16, max(2, header.length))`) while never capping header columns, and keep reporting the dropped cells in `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns`.
839.title: [Bug] One outlier line sets a delimited preview's width, so a two-column file renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns

840.author: HugoXK
840.body:
## What happens

The delimited-preview payload carries a `warnings: string[]` field that no consumer reads, and which duplicates text the client already composes and localizes.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): the `warnings` array is built at the end of `parseDelimitedTable` ("The file has {total} columns; the preview shows the first {shown}." and "{n} cells past the preview width are not shown.") and returned in the payload type (`:161`-ish in that revision).
- `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` mirrors the field in the web payload type.
- The viewer does not use it: `ArtifactModal` passes `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` down and `DatasetTable` composes its own sentences from `artifact.tableClippedColumns` / `artifact.tableClippedCells` (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`).

## Why it matters

Two places decide what the user is told about a clipped preview: the server strings are English-only, so a Chinese UI would drift from them the moment anyone read them, and a future consumer could show untranslated text. Today the field is dead weight in every preview payload.

## Suggested fix

Either drop `warnings` from the payload and keep `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` as the only source of truth (the client already localizes from them), or make the client render the server strings through the i18n layer. Pick one owner for the copy.
840.title: [Cleanup] The delimited preview payload's `warnings` field duplicates the client copy, is not localized, and has no consumer

841.author: HugoXK
841.body:
## What happens

`GET` artifact version preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `buildArtifactVersionPreview` → `parseDelimitedTable` / `recordArrayTable`) now bounds its payload with two server-side constants:

- `const maxRows = Math.min(MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS, parsePositiveInt(maxRowsParam, DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS));` — `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 100` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:719` at `0477d328`)
- `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS);` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:398`)

A caller that asks for more gets less, with no error: the response just carries `truncated` and `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells`.

## Measured at `0477d328`

- 1,500-column CSV → `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {shown 1001, total 1500}`, `clippedCells 499` (named columns past 1,001 are dropped).
- 401-row CSV at `?maxRows=400` → `rows 100`, `totalRows 400`, `truncated true`.
- 500-record JSON at `?maxRows=400` → the same 100 rows (the clamp applies to the record-array path too).

## Why it matters

The bundled web client never sends `maxRows` (`apps/web/src/api/artifacts.ts:201` forwards an optional value only, and `apps/desktop` reads local CSV), so there is no in-repo regression — but for any other API caller this is a silent contract change: asking for 400 rows returns 100, and a legitimately wide table loses named columns. `#829` asked for a preview that keeps every row as wide as the columns it advertises; the bound is what makes the payload finite, so the trade is deliberate — it is the *silence* that needs a decision.

Two questions to settle, and then to write down where a caller can find them:

1. Should `maxRows` above the server constant be rejected (400 with a stated limit) instead of clamped, or should `truncated` stay the only signal?
2. Should the preview document the row limit and the column limit (with `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells` as the reporting half) in the API docs, and should a caller be able to learn both limits without probing?

Related: `#829` (the shear this bound fixes), `#839` (the width rule taken from the widest line), `#840` (the payload `warnings` field has no consumer).

## Suggested fix

Decide the two questions above, then either reject over-limit `maxRows` with a stated maximum or document the clamp; document `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS` and `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` (and that a wider/taller request is clipped, not failed) in the API reference, so an outside caller can size its request without probing.
841.title: [Bug] The artifact preview endpoint silently clamps `?maxRows=` to 100 and caps the column set at 1,001, so an outside API caller gets less than it asked for

842.author: HugoXK
842.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview is capped at `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` columns and `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = 100` rows, and the payload reports what left the preview (`clippedColumns {total, shown}`, `clippedCells`, `warnings`). The viewer renders that report only through `DatasetTable` — and `.csv` artifacts never render `DatasetTable`.

## Where (at `981fdf51`, the merge commit of `#830`)

- `apps/web/src/csvArtifact.ts:73-82` — `detectCsvArtifact` sends every `.csv` name, `text/csv` media type or CSV-looking content to the CSV viewer.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:874` — `artifact?.kind === "dataset" && csvDetection && !(structureFormat && source)` renders `CsvArtifactPreview` (`:205`), not the dataset table.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:831-832` — `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns` are passed only to `DatasetTable` (`:239`, meta line at `:254`).
- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` — the JSON record-array path always returns `clippedCells: 0` and `clippedColumns {shown: total}`, so `.tsv` (and generally delimited content that is not detected as CSV) is the only kind whose clipped numbers reach a reader.

## Measured

- A `.csv` artifact with 200,001-field lines: the API preview comes back `1001` columns / `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 200001}`, and the artifact panel shows only the "open CSV workspace" card — none of the new text, because the CSV workspace parses the source client-side.
- The same content saved as `.tsv`: `DatasetTable` renders `1 row (showing 1001 of 200001 columns) (N cells past the preview width are not shown)`.

## Why it matters

`#830`'s stated contract is that clipping "is reported, not silent" — and for the most common delimited artifact kind (`.csv`) the reader is told nothing. The new i18n strings (`artifact.tableClippedColumns`, `artifact.tableClippedCells`) and the two props have no reachable CSV path.

## Suggested fix

Either pass the clipped numbers into `CsvArtifactPreview` / the CSV workspace window and render the same meta line there, or render the dataset table for a CSV artifact whose payload was clipped. One signal per loss, no duplicate sentences; keep the CSV workspace's own surplus-column handling (`csv.importSurplusColumns`) separate from this panel-level notice.

Related: `#839` (the width rule that creates the mismatch), `#840` (the payload `warnings` field has no consumer), `#841` (`maxRows` / column-cap contract for outside API callers).
842.title: [Bug] The clipped-preview notice never reaches `.csv` readers: the CSV panel renders no column or cell clip signal

844.author: nanzhaogang
844.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Both clients (`apps/web` and `apps/desktop`) can fail in ways a user cannot describe from memory: a stuck run, a wrong artifact, an offline shell. Today the only way to report one is to leave the app, open GitHub, and write an issue from scratch — which loses the version, OS, locale and the failure state the app itself already knows. Error surfaces (including the "cannot reach the local service" screen) end in a dead end with no way to say anything.

This issue tracks the full delivery: a shared submission contract, a Cloudflare Worker that relays reports into a private GitHub issue, a feedback dialog in both front ends, an entry point on the offline screen that seeds the dialog with the failure's diagnostics, and a receipt code the user can quote when following up.

Related: desktop coverage gap recorded as §12 of the feedback design doc (`用户反馈功能-方案.md`); the desktop shell must not be left out of a feature that only lands in `apps/web`.

Related pull request: branch `feat/user-feedback` — feature implementation, tests and deployment notes.

## Design Ideas

- **One contract, three consumers.** Payload building, redaction, PII detection, field validation and receipt generation live in `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts` and are imported by `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and the Worker. The wire format cannot drift between the two clients and the server.
- **Triage fields are required.** Frequency (always / sometimes / once) and impact (blocks me / slows my work / affects the experience) are mandatory: a report without them cannot be routed or prioritized, so the dialog keeps 提交 disabled and states why, rather than accepting an untriaged issue.
- **A receipt instead of an account.** A submission returns `FB-XXXX-XXXX`, drawn from a 32-symbol alphabet (no `I/O/0/1`) to stay readable over the phone. It is shown once, kept in local history, and is what support asks for.
- **Diagnostics on by default, redacted on the way out.** Key names are forced to `[REDACTED:key]`, Windows profile paths are normalized, and the user can uncheck the block. The offline screen pre-fills diagnostics with boot state, origin and user agent so a "cannot connect" report arrives with evidence attached.
- **PII is advisory, not a wall.** Phone numbers, ID cards and emails in the description raise a confirmation step instead of silently rewriting the text, because the user may be quoting exactly what broke.
- **Draft and history stay local.** The draft is written to `localStorage` on every change and restored on reopen; the last 50 submissions live beside it. Nothing is stored server-side except the issue itself.
- **Abuse control belongs to the relay, not the client.** Keyed dedupe for seven days, a per-IP hourly limit, a per-install daily limit and a daily issue quota keep a public endpoint from becoming a spam funnel — and a duplicate returns the original receipt instead of creating a second issue.
- **The token never ships.** The GitHub PAT lives as a Cloudflare secret; the bundle only knows the Worker URL.

## Involved Public APIs

One new endpoint, on the Worker (not on the product's REST service): `POST /api/feedback`.

- Request: `{ kind, title, body, contact?, meta, diagnostics? }`; `kind ∈ {bug, idea, other}`, body 10–2000 characters, title capped at 120, diagnostics capped at 4000, whole request capped at 16 KiB.
- Response `201 { receipt, createdAt, issueUrl? }`; failures are `400 invalid`, `403 origin`, `409 duplicate` (carries the original receipt), `413 too_large`, `429 rate_limited`, `502 upstream`, `503 unavailable`.
- CORS: an explicit origin allowlist, configurable through `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, covering the local dev ports of both clients.
- Endpoint constant: `FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` / `FEEDBACK_API_PATH` in `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`.

No route of `services/api` changes; the clients do not proxy feedback through the local backend, so reporting still works when the backend is down.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/operational-logging`: new `feedback` entry point (contract, validation, redaction, receipts, PII) and its reuse of the existing `redaction` and `diagnostics` helpers.
- `packages/feedback-worker`: new workspace package — Worker entry, GitHub issue creation, KV-backed limits, mock-GitHub tests.
- `apps/web`: dialog, API client mapping status codes to user-facing failures, draft/history store, entries in the header and in `ErrorDiagnosticActions`.
- `apps/desktop`: the same dialog and store, a 我要反馈 entry in the sidebar footer to the right of the GitHub star, and an entry on the offline screen that pre-fills diagnostics; the dialog is mounted in the offline branch so that entry works.
- Internationalization: every string lands in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` and in both `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` and `en.ts`; the two dictionaries must stay structurally identical.
- Infrastructure: a `FEEDBACK_KV` namespace and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret on Cloudflare; labels `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>`, `needs-triage` on created issues.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests (47 cases across 6 files):**
  - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.test.ts` (8): receipt format and 100k uniqueness, redaction of keyed values and profile paths, advisory PII detection, contact classification, title derivation, payload building, field validation.
  - `packages/feedback-worker/src/index.test.ts` (9): CORS preflight and disallowed origin, 16 KiB rejection before parsing, 400 on bad JSON/fields, success path creating an issue, 409 duplicate within the window, per-install daily 429, daily quota 503, GitHub 5xx surfacing 502 without leaking the token.
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackApi.test.ts` (8) and `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-submit.test.ts` (8): status-code to failure mapping in each client.
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackStore.test.ts` (7) and `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-store.test.ts` (7): install id persistence, draft default and round-trip, corrupt-data fallback, history capped at 50, removal by receipt.
- **Component tests:** not yet written. The required-field rule (`frequency` and `impact` both chosen before submit) is currently covered by manual verification only; the plan is to extract the form-state predicate out of the dialog into a shared pure function and assert it from both apps.
- **End-to-end (manual, against the deployed Worker):** submit from the desktop dialog → receipt shown and recorded in 我的反馈; stop the local backend, reload, land on the offline screen → 我要反馈 → description pre-filled and diagnostics expandable → submit → receipt; restart the backend → 重试 recovers in one click. Verified receipts: `FB-775M-N8A8` (normal), `FB-XKXW-FGSZ` (from the offline screen).
- **Regression:** the offline screen still renders exactly as before when no feedback is submitted; ordinary sessions are untouched; the web feedback dialog behaves identically to the desktop one.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (architecture check, typecheck, unit tests); `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test`; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report can be submitted from `apps/web` and from `apps/desktop`, and a GitHub issue is created with `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>` and `needs-triage`.
- [ ] Frequency and impact are mandatory in both clients: an untouched form keeps 提交 disabled and shows 出现频率和影响程度为必填项.
- [ ] The receipt shown after submission matches the one in 我的反馈 and the issue body.
- [ ] The offline screen's 我要反馈 opens the dialog with the failure text pre-filled and diagnostics available (not "本条反馈没有可用诊断信息").
- [ ] A submission from the offline screen still succeeds while the local backend is down.

## Additional Information

Deployed endpoint: `https://sciencediscovery-feedback.sciencediscovery.workers.dev` (Cloudflare requires the `<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` form). KV namespace `FEEDBACK_KV`; secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `REPO_OWNER`, `REPO_NAME`; deployment via `npx wrangler deploy` from `packages/feedback-worker`. Deployment and verification steps are in `packages/feedback-worker/README.md`; the design document is `用户反馈功能-方案.md` (§11 review revisions, §12 desktop coverage).

---

## 🚀 背景描述

两端客户端（`apps/web` 与 `apps/desktop`）都会出现用户无法靠记忆描述清楚的故障：运行卡住、产物不对、本地服务连不上。今天要反馈这类问题，用户必须先离开应用、打开 GitHub、从零写一个 issue——版本、系统、语言、当时的故障状态全部丢失，而这些信息应用本身就有。报错界面（包括「连不上本地服务」那一页）是个死胡同，用户没有地方说一句话。

本 issue 跟踪完整交付：共享的提交契约、把反馈转成私有 GitHub issue 的 Cloudflare Worker、两端一致的反馈对话框、在离线页把故障诊断预填进对话框的入口，以及用户可以引用的回执码。

相关：桌面端覆盖缺口记录在反馈方案文档 `用户反馈功能-方案.md` 的 §12；一个只落在 `apps/web` 的功能，不应把桌面端漏掉。

相关 PR：分支 `feat/user-feedback`——功能实现、测试与部署说明。

## 设计思路

- **一份契约、三个使用方。** payload 构造、脱敏、PII 检测、字段校验与回执生成集中在 `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`，由 `apps/web`、`apps/desktop` 与 Worker 共同引用，两端与服务的线上格式不会漂移。
- **分诊字段必填。** 出现频率（总是 / 偶尔 / 仅一次）与影响程度（无法使用 / 影响工作效率 / 影响使用体验）为必填项：缺少这两项的报告无法定级与派发，因此对话框在未选时保持「提交」禁用并说明原因，而不是收下一条无法分诊的 issue。
- **用回执码，而不是账号。** 提交返回 `FB-XXXX-XXXX`，字符集剔除 `I/O/0/1` 以便口头转述；提交成功时展示一次，并保留在本地历史里，客服只需要这个码。
- **诊断信息默认附带、出口前脱敏。** 键名强制为 `[REDACTED:key]`，Windows 用户目录路径归一化，用户可以取消勾选。离线页会自动带上启动状态、origin 与 user agent，让「连不上」这类报告自带证据。
- **PII 只提示、不拦截。** 描述里的手机号、身份证、邮箱触发一次确认，而不是偷偷改写文本——用户可能正是在引用出错的内容。
- **草稿与历史留在本地。** 草稿随输入写入 `localStorage`，下次打开恢复；最近 50 条提交记录与之并列。服务端除 issue 本身外不存任何内容。
- **限流属于中继，不属于客户端。** 七天内的去重、按 IP 的小时限流、按 installId 的日限流与每日 issue 配额，防止公开端点变成垃圾入口；重复内容返回原回执码，不再开第二个 issue。
- **Token 永不进包。** GitHub PAT 存在 Cloudflare secret 里，前端只知道 Worker 地址。

## 涉及的公共 API

新增一个端点，位于 Worker（不落在产品 REST 服务上）：`POST /api/feedback`。

- 请求：`{ kind, title, body, contact?, meta, diagnostics? }`；`kind ∈ {bug, idea, other}`，正文 10–2000 字，标题上限 120，诊断上限 4000，整个请求上限 16 KiB。
- 响应 `201 { receipt, createdAt, issueUrl? }`；失败为 `400 invalid`、`403 origin`、`409 duplicate`（带原回执码）、`413 too_large`、`429 rate_limited`、`502 upstream`、`503 unavailable`。
- CORS：显式 origin 白名单，可通过 `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` 配置，默认覆盖两端本地开发端口。
- 端点常量：`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts` 中的 `FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` / `FEEDBACK_API_PATH`。

`services/api` 的路由不变；两端不经过本地后端转发反馈，因此本地服务挂掉时仍可提交。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/operational-logging`：新增 `feedback` 入口（契约、校验、脱敏、回执、PII），复用既有的 `redaction` 与 `diagnostics`。
- `packages/feedback-worker`：新增 workspace 包——Worker 入口、GitHub issue 创建、KV 限流、基于 mock GitHub 的测试。
- `apps/web`：对话框、把状态码映射为用户可读失败原因的 API 客户端、草稿/历史存储、头部入口与 `ErrorDiagnosticActions` 中的入口。
- `apps/desktop`：同一套对话框与存储、侧栏底部 GitHub 星标右侧的「我要反馈」入口，以及离线页上预填诊断的入口；对话框在离线分支同样挂载，保证该入口可用。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` 与 `apps/desktop` 的 `text/zh.ts`、`en.ts`，两份字典结构必须完全一致。
- 基础设施：Cloudflare 上的 `FEEDBACK_KV` namespace 与 `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret；新建 issue 打上 `source:in-app`、`kind:<kind>`、`needs-triage` 标签。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试（6 个文件、47 个用例）：**
  - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.test.ts`（8）：回执码格式与 10 万次唯一性、键值脱敏与路径归一化、PII 提示不改原文、联系方式分类、标题推导、payload 构造、字段校验。
  - `packages/feedback-worker/src/index.test.ts`（9）：CORS 预检与非法来源、解析前拒绝 16 KiB、非法 JSON/字段 400、成功建 issue、窗口内重复 409、installId 日限 429、每日配额 503、GitHub 5xx 返回 502 且不泄露 token。
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackApi.test.ts`（8）与 `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-submit.test.ts`（8）：两端各自的状态码到失败类型映射。
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackStore.test.ts`（7）与 `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-store.test.ts`（7）：installId 持久化、草稿默认值与往返、脏数据回退、历史上限 50、按回执码删除。
- **组件测试：** 尚未编写。必填项规则（未选出现频率与影响程度时不可提交）目前只有人工验证覆盖；计划把对话框里的表单状态判断抽成共享纯函数，两端各写断言。
- **端到端（人工，对已部署 Worker）：** 桌面端对话框提交 → 展示回执码且「我的反馈」有记录；停掉本地后端并刷新 → 进入离线页 →「我要反馈」→ 描述已预填、诊断可展开 → 提交 → 得到回执码；恢复后端 → 点「重试」一次即恢复。已验证回执码：`FB-775M-N8A8`（正常）、`FB-XKXW-FGSZ`（离线页）。
- **回归：** 不提交反馈时离线页与改动前完全一致；普通会话不受影响；Web 与桌面端对话框行为一致。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（架构检查、类型检查、单元测试）；`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test`；`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`。

## 验收标准

- [ ] `apps/web` 与 `apps/desktop` 均可提交反馈，并创建带 `source:in-app`、`kind:<kind>`、`needs-triage` 的 GitHub issue。
- [ ] 两端的出现频率与影响程度均为必填：未选择时「提交」保持禁用，并显示「出现频率和影响程度为必填项」。
- [ ] 提交后展示的回执码与「我的反馈」记录、issue 正文中的一致。
- [ ] 离线页的「我要反馈」打开对话框时描述已预填，诊断信息可用（不是「本条反馈没有可用诊断信息」）。
- [ ] 本地后端停止时，从离线页提交仍然成功。

## 补充信息

已部署端点：`https://sciencediscovery-feedback.sciencediscovery.workers.dev`（Cloudflare 固定为 `<worker>.<子域名>.workers.dev` 形式）。KV namespace `FEEDBACK_KV`；secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`、`REPO_OWNER`、`REPO_NAME`；在 `packages/feedback-worker` 下执行 `npx wrangler deploy` 部署。部署与验证步骤见 `packages/feedback-worker/README.md`；方案文档为 `用户反馈功能-方案.md`（§11 评审修订、§12 桌面端覆盖）。

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Deleting a model is rejected if an existing session references it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a session using a configured model.
2. Try to delete that model.
3. Deletion is rejected because the model is used by the session.

**Expected behavior**

Allow the model configuration to be deleted without deleting historical sessions. Preserve session history; if a user resumes an affected session, prompt them to select an available model.

ScienceDiscovery Web UI.

Not specified.

This behavior is included in the v0.4.0-rc1 release scope: #718.
